_comment: Client mods the launcher can turn on and off, and what to call them.
_comment2: A mod is toggleable exactly when VanillaFixes injects it from the client's own dlls.txt, so the file name here has to match a line in there. Anything in a client's dlls.txt that is NOT listed here still appears in the launcher, named after its file: a client may carry a mod we have never heard of, and hiding it would leave no way to turn it off.
_comment3: The notes are hand written and are what a player reads, so keep them short and free of dashes. Correct one rather than leaving it vague.
_comment4: dxvk does NOT belong here. It loads by sitting beside WoW.exe as d3d9.dll and friends, not from dlls.txt, and Turtle ships the d3d9 one itself. Its row is `dxvk` in packages.json. See docs/notes/launcher-client-toggles.md.
_comment5: url/sha256/version are how a mod the client does NOT have gets fetched. The url is always the upstream project's own release asset: nothing here is rehosted, and `from` is the project it belongs to. Five of the six are in a stock Turtle client already, so in practice this fetches Interact and repairs a deleted file, and never upgrades anything.
_comment6: EVERY sha256 WAS MEASURED AGAINST THE FILE ALREADY IN THE CLIENT, on 2026-09-20: each pinned asset is byte identical to what octow and clean-turtle carry. That is the whole reason these pins are safe. Re-measure before moving one to a newer version, and say what changed.
_comment6b: Lexara and ClassicAPI (added 2026-09-21) are the exception: no client here has either, so there was nothing to compare against. Their pins are our own hash of the downloaded asset, which matched the digest GitHub publishes for it. Both were releasing more than once a day when pinned, and the launcher never upgrades a file that is already there, so a newer pin reaches only clients that do not have the mod yet.
_comment7: No `extract` means the download IS the file and is written to `file`. With `extract` the download is a zip and each key is an entry in it: a key ending in / takes that whole subtree, anything else is one file. The value is where it goes, relative to the client.
_comment8: A bundled addon is a decision, not a default. Turtle injects UnitXP_SP3.dll WITHOUT UnitXP_SP3_Addon, so taking that subtree would add something a stock client does not have. Interact is the other way: its addon carries Bindings.xml, so without it there is no key to press.
_comment10: variant: true is another build of a file an earlier entry already names, and it gets a row of its own that says which build is on disk. file_sha256 is the hash of that file AS IT LANDS, which is how the launcher tells the two builds apart, since the name is the same. Unticking a variant puts the plain entry's build back and deletes the variant's other files, so the plain entry must carry a url. It never touches dlls.txt: the plain entry's row stays the on/off switch for the line, whichever build it loads. Anything else the zip holds is left out by naming only what we want, which matters for VanillaHelpers64, whose TexBridgeFullLog.txt switches on verbose logging just by existing.
_comment12: also lists more downloads that come with a mod, each with url, sha256 and extract: an addon kept in a repo of its own. A mod whose DLL is on the disk and whose addon or ini is not reads reinstall.
_comment11: section names the heading the C# launcher draws the row under, after Game fixes. Absent means Game fixes. A mod from github.com/aloofbit goes under ComfyCraft whatever it says.
_comment9: inject: false means the file is fetched but never written into dlls.txt. VanillaFixes is the only one: it IS the injector, so a checkbox for it would be a switch for the thing that reads the switches. IchaLaunch draws the same line, by leaving the dlls_txt key off that one entry. Such a row is offered only on a client that does not have it, because once it does there is nothing to toggle.

_why: Added 2026-09-24. VanillaFixes loads SuperWoWhook.dll from dlls.txt (pepopo978/SuperwowInstallation, step 7B), so SuperWoWlauncher.exe is not needed and not taken. octow's copy is byte identical to this zip's. The sha256 matched the digest GitHub publishes. THE TAG `Release` IS REUSED: the author replaces the zip under it (this one holds files dated 2026-07-16 in a release from 2025-02-01), so a new upload fails the hash check and the install stops without changing anything. Re-pin then. The licence is personal use only and forbids distribution; the launcher fetches the author's own release and hosts nothing. The companion addon SuperAPI (the default UI's compatibility, and a minimap menu for SuperWoW's settings) has no releases, so `also` fetches GitHub's archive of one commit; two downloads of it hashed the same.

Its four bundle only modules (framecrash, outline, interact, dpslog) are left out with it.

_why: Our own three, added 2026-09-21 and re-pinned 2026-09-22 to that day's releases: comfygrass, comfyatmosphere (comfyfog.dll) and comfytime. comfygrass was re-pinned again on 2026-09-23 to v0.2.1-alpha, which makes rain show again, and comfyatmosphere the same day to v0.4.1-alpha, which adds its controls to Video > Shaders, removes the sun rays, and keeps the addon silent when the DLL is turned off. v0.4.0-alpha was pinned for one commit and never deployed; its addon printed a chat line at every login once the launcher had turned the DLL off. comfyatmosphere was re-pinned on 2026-09-24 to v0.5.0-alpha, which brings the sun rays back, adds a Volumetric Light Quality control, stops the light jittering while walking, and makes it cheaper. It was re-pinned on 2026-09-25 to v0.5.1-alpha, which makes the volumetric light work with anti-aliasing (multisampling) on. It was re-pinned the same day to v0.5.2-alpha, which keeps buildings and ground in the shadow map after the player has seen more than copyMax of them. Then to v0.5.3-alpha, which halves the light's CPU cost, stops the light through trees jittering while walking, and frees depth stand-ins left behind by a window resize. Then to v0.5.4-alpha, which stops a resolution change or a Maximized toggle from scrambling the screen or crashing the game (ERROR #124): the client makes a new device for those, and the mod kept using what it had made on the old one. On 2026-09-28 it was re-pinned to v0.6.0-alpha, which adds Night Strength (the rays and the light at night), follows the moons at night, and fades the rays and the light when terrain covers the sun. On 2026-09-30 it was re-pinned to v0.7.0-alpha, which adds sun shadows from the map files, glowing lamps, candles and fireplaces, Night Darkness and Moonlight Colour, and a settings window (/atmos options) for clients without the Atmosphere page; and again the same day to v0.8.0-alpha, which adds the volumetric fog, stops shadows blinking in Stormwind, and adds a debug panel (/atmos debug). It was re-pinned the same day to v0.8.1-alpha, which gives the shadows their own night share (Night Shadows), so the moon casts them, and makes the shadows of players and creatures darker than the world's (Character Shadow Strength). Then the same day to v0.8.2-alpha, which keeps shadows on their casters when the sun or moon is low: the shadows' light climbs back toward overhead as the real light sets. Then the same day to v0.8.3-alpha, which brings the sun shadows back in Stormwind's Trade District, removes a shadow cast from the empty sky over it, and adds Sun Smoothing. Then on 2026-10-01 to v0.8.4-alpha, which lights many more lamps, torches and candles in their own flame's colour (Stormwind's street lamps and NPCs' torches among them), stops lamps going dark as you turn or walk up, adds Lantern Light, Torch Light, Indoor Lamps and Lamps by Day, and puts /atmos options in sections. Then the same day to v0.8.5-alpha, which lights the torches some NPCs carry (the client sends them black) and makes the lamps' defaults dimmer. Then the same day to v0.8.6-alpha, which lays the fog on the floor of cities under the ground (Ironforge, the Undercity, mines), starts the effects at once at a login indoors, gives bear and travel form their shadows, takes a player's shadow off the water under a bridge, and writes a report of the client into comfyfog.log. Then the same day to v0.8.7-alpha, which gives each character one shadow that reaches its feet, stops the shade on a character's back stepping and flickering, sharpens the shadows near you, and adds Character Backside Shadow. Then on 2026-10-02 to v0.9.0-alpha, which lets the fog draw with Volumetric Light off, holds shadow edges still as you walk, keeps close-cast shade (merlons, eaves) past the near map with a middle shadow map, shows a tree's shadow inside a hill's, keeps banners, statues and a paladin's mount solid, and adds Near Shadow Distance and Tree Shadow Strength. comfygrass was re-pinned the same day to v0.2.2-alpha for the same fault: it kept the old device's wind shader. comfytime was re-pinned the same day to v0.3.0-alpha, which adds Ctrl+End to switch between day and night. Every pin is our own hash of a fresh download of the release asset, and each matched the sha256 digest GitHub publishes for it. A client that already carries one of them gets an unticked `update` row when its pin moves, found by file_sha256. They coordinate among themselves at start up (each waits for the others to finish patching the Direct3D device), so the order the launcher appends their dlls.txt lines in does not matter. All three are alpha and ask for a backup first. On 2026-10-06 comfygrass became part of comfyatmosphere (v0.10.0-alpha), whose DLL is comfyatmos.dll from that release, with comfyatmos.ini: the Swaying grass row was removed, and this entry names comfygrass's and comfyfog's files in supersedes_files and the ComfyGrass addon in supersedes, so the update takes the old DLLs out of dlls.txt and sets their files aside (launcher v1.21). comfyatmosphere was re-pinned to v0.10.0-alpha, which adds the water, the grass in the wind, lighthouses, a Color tab and Rain Darkness; comfytime to v0.3.1-alpha and comfyaim to v0.1.4-alpha, which wait for comfyatmos.dll to finish patching as they waited for comfyfog.dll. comfyatmosphere was re-pinned on 2026-10-07 to v0.11.0-alpha: the volumetric light costs about 40% less; the ini adds three keys with built-in values. comfyatmosphere was re-pinned later on 2026-10-07 to v0.11.1-alpha: water fixes (the split where a lake meets the sea, the wet sand on steep banks, a swimmer's camera inside a wave) and a Wet Sand slider. comfyatmosphere was re-pinned later on 2026-10-07 to v0.11.2-alpha: the game's own lighthouse light is left out again in Stormwind's harbour, a Lighthouse Distance slider, and the beam's light on the water ends where the beam ends; the ini adds one key with a built-in value. comfyatmosphere was re-pinned later on 2026-10-07 to v0.11.3-alpha: creatures and objects under the water no longer show as flat, pale shapes (the fog, the volumetric light and the sun shadows stop at the water's surface); the ini changes only a comment. On 2026-10-07 comfytime became part of comfyatmosphere (v0.12.0-alpha): the Time of day row was removed, and this entry names comfytime.dll and comfytime.ini in supersedes_files, so the update takes comfytime.dll out of dlls.txt and sets both files aside. comfyatmosphere v0.12.0-alpha also puts every action in Key Bindings, turns off the keys it read past the game's bindings, and adds a time slider and Lock time to its debug panel; the ini adds a [time] section and three [general] keys, each with a built-in value. comfyatmosphere was re-pinned on 2026-10-12 to v0.13.0-alpha: its own clouds in place of the game's cloud layer, the water at about one and a half times the frame rate, a river that climbs drawn to its far end, and a ring where someone lands in the water. The ini adds a [clouds] section and keys in [sky] and [water], each with a built-in value; an old ini keeps clouds = 0, so its clouds stay off until Clouds is ticked. comfyatmosphere was re-pinned later on 2026-10-12 to v0.13.1-alpha: water inside a building (a dungeon's lake, Stormwind's canals) takes its height from the files instead of a read of the client's buffers in each frame, which took a lake in Grand Moo Canyon from 187 to 16 frames a second; the canals no longer keep another map's water colour. The addon and the ini did not change. comfyatmosphere was re-pinned later on 2026-10-12 to v0.14.0-alpha: a Time section in /atmos options with Server time, Computer time (from nummy, pull request 10) and Fixed hour, and the server's time shown again at once when the time is no longer fixed. The DLL adds the new [time] localTime key to an old ini when Computer time is first chosen. comfyatmosphere was re-pinned on 2026-10-15 to v0.15.0-alpha: the sun and the moons from the game clock, so the shadows no longer turn with the camera; Highest Sun (80) and Low Sun From; the near shadow maps at least 2048; a player's shadow whole down a slope; spells drawn over the shadows and the fog; Zone Saturation, Zone Hue and Wet Sand Distance for the water; Game Glow (80). The ini adds [sunshadows] highest and [colour] gameGlow, each with a built-in value. comfyatmosphere was re-pinned on 2026-10-16 to v0.16.0-alpha: the water's colour from the game's light tables (Water Saturation 145 replaces Zone Saturation; Zone Colour, Zone Hue and Water Colour removed); the AMD water bands (#11) and the swell's triangles fixed; a wall's lit foot fixed; spells drawn in the game's order again; Highest Sun 65 and Game Glow 15 by default. An old ini keeps 80, 80 and 1.65.
name: Fog and light
note: volumetric fog, sun shadows, glowing lamps, darker nights, water, grass in the wind, light through the trees, and the time of day
_extract_comment: The addon is the controls on Video > Atmosphere, and the /atmos options window. It reads CVars that the DLL registers, so it adds nothing when the DLL is not loaded. The ini comes along, and must: v0.5.0-alpha changed its defaults (shadow map size, samples, redraw rate, smoothing) and brought back the [rays] section, and an old ini's values override the new defaults, so a client that kept it would not get the lower cost. v0.7.0-alpha changed the defaults again (the game's own fog by default, the owner's slider values) and added keys. v0.8.0-alpha replaced the [fog] section with the new fog's keys and changed the light's defaults; its Bindings.xml puts the probe, the stats and the debug panel in Key Bindings. v0.8.1-alpha added [sunshadows] night, unitStrength and unitGap. v0.8.2-alpha added riseFrom and riseTo and changed unitGap to 0.5. v0.8.3-alpha added [sun] glide. v0.8.4-alpha added [lamps] torchLight, lanternLight and indoors, raised maxLights to 32 and changed the lamps' defaults. v0.8.5-alpha changed strength, torchLight and lanternLight. v0.10.0-alpha renamed the files comfyatmos.dll and comfyatmos.ini, and added [water], [lighthouse], [colour] and [grass].

_extract_comment: NO ini, on purpose. comfyaim.ini holds the player's secret, which is what proves their nick is theirs, and an update rewrites every file named here: shipping the ini would sign every updated player on as nobody, with their nick lost to them. The DLL's built-in defaults are the ini's (live hub, on), and it writes the file itself when it first saves a nick. The addon is /a, the window and the friends list button; the DLL does nothing visible without it.

_why: Added 2026-10-08: comfylogin's DLL. The Saved accounts row in packages.json brings patch-W and needs this row. The DLL keeps the list in WTF\comfylogin.txt, encrypts the passwords with DPAPI, and turns off the stock exe's GlueXML check. The release asset is one zip with comfylogin.dll and Data/patch-W.mpq; only the DLL is taken here, and the package row takes the patch. The pin is our own hash of the asset, and it matched the digest GitHub publishes for it. Hidden since 2026-10-14, the owner's call: two ticks for one feature confused players. The C# launcher draws no row for it, lists its file under Saved accounts, and turns it on and off with that row.

note: keeps the saved accounts list and its passwords
